newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to float 20 pct of Maghrebail.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to float 20 pct of Maghrebail.

text.p: Morocco will float on the Casablanca stock exchange 20 percent of the credit firm Maghrebail worth 82 million dirhams ($8.7 million), the firm's chairman Mohamed Amin Benjelloun said on Tuesday.
"We decided to float 205,064 shares of Maghrebail at 400 dirhams per share on the bourse by the end of June," Benjelloun told a news conference.
Subscription, which will also be open to foreign investors, was set from June 30 to July 4, he said.
Shares will be offered in two categories. One tranche of 102,532 shares will be offered to the general public including foreign investors. Another similar tranche will be devoted to institutions.
Maghrebail showed 22 million dirhams net profit in 1996 compared with 25.4 million dirhams in the previous year.
Benjelloun said the firm held a 23.6 percent share of Morocco's leasing market in 1996.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc and Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur hold respectively 27.5 percent and 11.8 percent of Maghrebail.
Established in 1972, the firm has a capital of 64.8 million dirhams divided in a nominal value of 100 dirhams per share.
The firm is expected to be listed on the stock exchange on July 10, 1997, the chairman added.
